scope: Brand travel and honeymoon facts reused from the parent article's packs (travel-advisor-wedding 02-research-A.json and 02-research-B.json), plus official Australian Government facts on passports, name change, visas, health and Smartraveller subscription. FAST mode, one round.
method_note: Reused facts were read live by the parent run on 2026-11-15 via Apify web-fetch and are copied with their sources. New facts were fetched in full today via Apify web-fetch from smartraveller.gov.au and passports.gov.au. No competitor, aggregator or site/ draft used.

facts.claim: The live travel page is branded Wedded Wonderland Travel and positions the service as a destination wedding travel agent.
facts.page_wording: Wedded Wonderland Travel. # Destination wedding travel agent

facts.claim: The travel service covers weddings, honeymoons and the trips in between, from first idea to homecoming.
facts.page_wording: For every celebration - weddings, honeymoons and the trips in between. The stays, the perks and the support behind every Wedded Wonderland journey, from first idea to homecoming.

facts.claim: Travel enquiries start through the 'Start planning' form on /travel: send dates and destination and the team comes back with a shortlist, the rates and exactly what is included.
facts.page_wording: Send us your dates and destination and we will come back with a shortlist, the rates and exactly what is included.

facts.claim: Step one takes about fifteen minutes, with no obligation and no cost to ask.
facts.page_wording: Step one takes about fifteen minutes, and there is no obligation to go further. ... No obligation, no cost to ask.

facts.claim: The process runs in five steps: tell us about the travel, agree the scope, receive a shortlist, book and brief the venue, and ongoing support.
facts.page_wording: Tell us about the travel ... We agree the scope ... You receive a shortlist ... We book and brief the venue ... We stay with you

facts.claim: The shortlist gives two or three options with a clear recommendation, the rate, the cancellation terms and the confirmed inclusions.
facts.page_wording: Two or three options with a clear recommendation, the rate, the cancellation terms and the confirmed inclusions.

facts.claim: Scope can be hotel only, the full celebration week, guest travel, honeymoon or all of it, and any planning fee is disclosed before work starts.
facts.page_wording: Hotel only, the full celebration week, guest travel, honeymoon or all of it. If any planning fee applies, you know before we start.

facts.claim: Fee line, quote exactly: a straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee; more complex itineraries, flights or group work may carry a fee agreed upfront.
facts.page_wording: A straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee. More complex itineraries, flights or group work may carry a fee, agreed with you upfront before any work begins.
facts.use_note: No fee amount is published. Do not quote a figure or say the service is free.

facts.claim: Eligible bookings may include daily breakfast, a hotel credit, room upgrade priority, early check-in and late checkout, a welcome amenity, preferred rates and offers, VIP recognition, and extras such as transfers, onboard credit, spa or club access.
facts.page_wording: Daily breakfast ... Hotel credit ... Room upgrade priority ... Early check-in, late checkout ... Welcome amenity ... Preferred rates and offers ... VIP recognition ... Extras beyond the room: Depending on the booking: transfers, onboard credit, spa or club access, exclusive experiences.
facts.use_note: Always 'may include', never 'includes'. Pair with F-010. These are the perks marketed as Wonderland Benefits (name on /wonderland-concierge); do not use 'Wedded Privileges'.

facts.claim: Inclusions vary by hotel, rate and dates, and the team confirms in writing what applies before booking; upgrades and early or late check times depend on occupancy and are shown as requests, not confirmed inclusions.
facts.page_wording: Inclusions vary by hotel, rate and dates - we confirm exactly what applies to your stay in writing before you book. ... We will always show you which inclusions are confirmed and which are requests
facts.use_note: /wonderland-concierge says 'Guaranteed late checkout'; follow the more cautious /travel wording (parent need N-006).

facts.claim: Wonderland Benefits apply at partner, preferred and consortia properties, vary by hotel and program, and are confirmed before the couple commits.
facts.page_wording: Benefits apply at our partner, preferred and consortia properties and vary by hotel and by program. Properties outside these networks may not carry the same perks. Your concierge confirms exactly what your chosen venue includes before you commit.

facts.claim: Wedded Wonderland offers one dedicated point of contact, with wedding, guest travel and honeymoon under one roof.
facts.page_wording: One Dedicated Point of Contact: No juggling multiple suppliers, planners or travel agents. ... Wedding + Travel Under One Roof: We manage your wedding, guest travel and honeymoon experience.

facts.claim: The team compares like for like (same room, taxes and cancellation terms) and will say if booking direct genuinely serves the client better; preferred rates are often the hotel's own flexible rate with perks added.
facts.page_wording: Preferred rates are often the same as the hotel's own flexible rate, with the perks added on top. We will always compare like for like - same room, same taxes, same cancellation terms - and tell you if booking direct genuinely serves you better.

facts.claim: The travel page asks clients for honesty about budget, a decision timeline, and any accessibility, allergy or dietary needs, and asks whether either partner holds hotel loyalty status or points.
facts.page_wording: Honesty about budget, a decision timeline, and any accessibility, allergy or dietary needs in your party. ... Do either of you hold hotel loyalty status or points worth using?

facts.claim: Perks usually cannot be added to a booking already made elsewhere; rebooking is considered only where it leaves the client better off.
facts.page_wording: Usually not to an existing booking made elsewhere. If the dates are still flexible and the rate is still available, we can look at rebooking - but only where it leaves you better off overall.
facts.use_note: Supports 'tell the advisor about existing bookings'.

facts.claim: Recommended lead time for a honeymoon is 6 to 9 months to lock in the right suite category (12 to 18 months for a destination wedding).
facts.page_wording: For a destination wedding, 12-18 months is the comfortable lead time ... For a honeymoon, 6-9 months is ideal to lock in the right suite category
facts.use_note: Parent pack sourced this to /destination-packages, not /destination-honeymoon-packages. Cite /destination-packages.

facts.claim: Every honeymoon package includes the suite category secured at the right rate, airport transfers and in-resort logistics, signature dining, spa, a private excursion and a dedicated specialist from enquiry to arrival.
facts.page_wording: Your suite category, secured at the right rate. Airport transfers and in-resort logistics. Signature dining and private reservations. A spa ritual or two, booked in advance. A private excursion that captures the place. A dedicated specialist from enquiry to arrival.

facts.claim: Wedding and honeymoon can be planned together, at one resort or two (or by extending the same stay), with one specialist coordinating the whole trip.
facts.page_wording: We can stage the wedding at one resort and the honeymoon at another (or extend the same stay), with one specialist coordinating the whole trip
facts.use_note: Supports the 'gap after the wedding' section.

facts.claim: The honeymoon page says the team never discounts its properties but negotiates value in upgrades and experiences.
facts.page_wording: we never discount our properties; we negotiate value instead, in upgrades and experiences.
facts.use_note: Do NOT use the US$1,600 to US$30,000+ range on the same page (unsourced, USD; flagged for Nic in parent). Line usable with Nic's OK.

facts.claim: Smartraveller says the right travel insurance is as essential as a passport for overseas travel, for every traveller.
Always read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) before buying; it sets out inclusions, exclusions, definitions, the claims process and emergency support.

Choose a policy covering every country on the trip including stopovers and transit points, check the destination is not at 'Do not travel', and check whether cancellation is covered if the advice level rises after booking.
Insurers exclude many activities from standard policies (even common ones such as cruises), so check the included and excluded activities list.
Travellers must tell their insurer about all pre-existing health conditions; most policies have an age limit.
Policies often limit each valuable item's value; check item limits and the excess.
facts.use_note: Relevant to rings and honeymoon valuables.

facts.claim: Free credit card travel insurance often covers fewer situations with lower item limits and usually has to be activated.
Travel insurance can cover cancellation costs if plans change; basic medical-only policies usually do not cover cancellation or property.
Medical assistance is usually the highest unexpected cost for Australians overseas, and the Australian Government cannot pay travellers' bills.
Smartraveller's essentials checklist says to confirm your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond the end of your trip.
facts.page_wording: Confirm your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond the end of your trip.

facts.claim: Smartraveller says some countries won't let you enter unless your passport is valid for six months after you plan to leave that country; some airlines impose this rule themselves; it can apply even when transiting or stopping over; it is applied inconsistently and getting it wrong can mean being stranded.
facts.page_wording: Some countries won't let you enter unless your passport is valid for six months after you plan to leave that country. Some airlines also impose this rule on their own initiative. It can apply even if you're just transiting or stopping over. Some foreign governments and airlines apply the rule inconsistently. You can receive conflicting advice from different sources. Getting it wrong can mean being stranded.
facts.use_note: Smartraveller says 'some countries', not 'many'. Write 'some countries' or follow the checklist rule in F-029. Same page's tips say 'at least six months from the date you will depart your destination'.

facts.claim: Allow at least 6 weeks to get a passport; where possible, don't book flights without a valid passport; faster processing may be available for urgent travel at an extra fee.
facts.page_wording: Allow at least 6 weeks to get your passport. Child applications can sometimes take longer. Where possible, don't book flights without a valid passport.

facts.claim: If you change your family name because of marriage, you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one, and the Australian Passport Office recommends booking travel in the name that is in your passport.
facts.page_wording: If you change your family name because of a change in your marital status, you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one. We recommend booking travel in the name that's in your passport.
facts.use_note: Key honeymoon point: book the honeymoon in the name on the passport you will carry. No date shown on page (last-modified header 2026-11-11).

facts.claim: To get a passport in a married name, the Passport Office needs documents linking the names: generally the Australian birth or citizenship certificate plus a marriage certificate issued by an Australian RBDM (or a registered relationship or RBDM name change certificate); Australians born in Australia who marry overseas always need a name change certificate.
facts.page_wording: You'll also need to show us either a: marriage certificate issued by an Australian RBDM ... There are certain circumstances where we'll always need a name change certificate. This applies to ... you were born in Australia and married or entered into a registered relationship overseas
facts.use_note: Relevant to destination weddings. A ceremonial certificate from a celebrant is not listed; only RBDM-issued documents are.

facts.claim: The replacement passport fee may be waived if the family name changed due to marriage and the current Australian passport expires more than 2 years from now, subject to other criteria.
facts.page_wording: You may be eligible to have the application fee for your replacement passport waived if you: changed your family name due to a change in marital status; hold a current Australian passport that expires more than 2 years from now.

facts.claim: Get the right visa for countries you are visiting or transiting through; visa conditions often change, so check with the embassy or consulate of your destinations before every trip.
facts.page_wording: Get the right visa for countries you're visiting or transiting through. Visa conditions often change, so check with the embassy or consulate of your destinations before every trip.

facts.claim: Smartraveller says it is the traveller's responsibility to have the right visa, visa rules can change at short notice, and Smartraveller cannot advise which visa you need; ask the destination's embassy or consulate.
facts.page_wording: It's your responsibility to make sure you have the right visa. Visa rules can change at short notice. Contact the embassy or consulate of the country you'll be visiting for advice specific to your needs.
facts.use_note: Frame visas as something to confirm with the official authority, not something the advisor guarantees.

facts.claim: Some countries require you to hand your passport to their officials for visa processing, during which you cannot travel; don't leave the application to the last minute. Use only authorised commercial visa services and watch for visa scams.
facts.page_wording: Some ask you to give your passport to their officials for processing. This could take some time. In the meantime, you won't have your passport and can't travel anywhere else. Don't leave your application to the last minute.

facts.claim: Getting the wrong visa or breaching its conditions can lead to jail, fines or deportation, and the Australian Government cannot tell you what visa to get.
facts.page_wording: Consequences can include: jail, fines, deportation. ... We can't tell you what visa to get.

facts.claim: Smartraveller advises talking to your doctor, finding out health risks at the destination, and getting a basic health check at least 8 weeks before you go, including recommended vaccinations.
facts.page_wording: Talk to your doctor. ... Find out if there are any health risks where you're going. Get a basic health check at least 8 weeks before you go. Get the recommended vaccinations.
facts.use_note: The vaccinations link on the page goes to vaccinehub.com.au (not government); cite the Smartraveller checklist, not that link.

facts.claim: Check your medication is legal and available at the destination, take enough for the whole trip, and carry copies of prescriptions and a doctor's letter.
facts.page_wording: Check if your medication is legal and available where you're going. Take enough of your prescribed medicines to last the whole trip. Carry copies of your prescription and a letter from your doctor.

facts.claim: Smartraveller no longer asks travellers to register trips; instead it offers a free email subscription for destination travel advice updates, news and a daily update, and encourages subscribing as soon as you are thinking about heading overseas.
facts.page_wording: We no longer ask you to register your trip with us before you travel. Instead, you can subscribe to get email updates and alerts from Smartraveller. ... We encourage you to subscribe as soon as you are thinking about heading overseas.
facts.use_note: Do NOT tell readers to 'register' with Smartraveller. Say 'subscribe'.

facts.claim: Subscribers must verify their email (link expires after one hour) and, if subscribing from the homepage, must choose destinations or they will receive no updates.
facts.page_wording: You must verify before you can receive alerts ... The verification link will expire after one hour ... If you don't do this step, you won't receive any updates.

facts.claim: Smartraveller advises photocopying the passport ID page, visa, prescriptions and insurance policy, leaving a copy with someone you trust, keeping hard copies of flight and accommodation bookings, and sharing your itinerary with friends or family.
facts.page_wording: Photocopy your passport ID page, visa and key documents ... Take a copy with you and leave one with someone you trust. Have hard copies of online flight, accommodation and event bookings ... Share your itinerary with friends or family members.

facts.claim: Australians, including dual nationals, should depart and enter Australia on their Australian passport.
facts.page_wording: Australians, including dual nationals, should depart and enter Australia on their Australian passport.
facts.use_note: Useful for multicultural couples: tell the advisor which passport each partner travels on.

price_note: No prices used. F-008 (fee line) has no figure. F-019 deliberately excludes the US$ range on the honeymoon page.

needs.need: Airline rules on a ticket name that differs from the passport: no official Australian Government page found; the Passport Office only recommends booking in the passport name (F-032). Airline-specific policy would need each carrier's own conditions.
Whether Wedded Wonderland Travel books flights and travel insurance for honeymoon clients (parent need N-013, collapsed FAQ not captured).

A real, anonymised honeymoon brief or client story showing what a good brief looked like and what the shortlist returned.

Resolve 'Guaranteed late checkout' (/wonderland-concierge) versus occupancy-dependent requests (/travel) (parent N-006).
Approval to use 'we never discount our properties; we negotiate value instead' (F-019).
